subject: Re: DPA — retention exemptions, legal-hold reconciliation & deletion certification
content:
--- Message 1/5 ---
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA questions: short-lived telemetry & legal hold carveouts

Sean —

Thanks for sending over the redline (attached). A couple of specific asks from LegalOps that we need clarity on before we can move to countersign:

1) Telemetry vs. customer-content retention: We need a carveout so operational telemetry (error rates, anonymized latency histograms) can be kept up to 90 days for debugging, but anything user-content should follow the standard erase window. Is that operationally feasible?

2) Backups: Acme is asking for a provision that backups may be kept up to 365 days for disaster recovery, but that certified deletion occurs within 30 days of a deletion request for primary storage — can you confirm how Redwood certifies deletion from backups?

3) Legal holds: if we receive a preservation notice, how do you reconcile that with standard erase windows? Specifically, how will you communicate hold lift/acknowledgement and the expected timeline for deletion when the hold is released?

Attached: Acme_DPA_redline_v3.pdf (redlines inline); legal requested a one-pager on the deletion certification flow if possible.

Appreciate a quick run — procurement is tracking.

—Sarah
Legal Operations, Acme Corp

To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: DPA questions: short-lived telemetry & legal hold carveouts

Thanks Sarah — looping in Karthik and Naomi to confirm operational and compliance impacts. High-level response: we can separate telemetry vs. content retention and implement a 90-day TTL for anonymized telemetry. Backups are trickier but we do support a certified deletion workflow for on-demand erasure events; need to confirm SLA language around backup snapshots. Legal holds are supported — they will suspend the deletion workflow and we provide evidence of hold receipt and release.

Next steps: Karthik — can you confirm the backup certification timeline and whether we can commit to "certified deletion of primary within 30 days, backup scrub within 90 days after removal from rotation"? Naomi — from compliance POV, is that acceptable or do you want tighter language?

Sean Gallagher
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

--- Message 3/5 ---
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2029 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions: short-lived telemetry & legal hold carveouts

Sarah / Sean —

Operational details from infra:
- Telemetry: we tag operational telemetry at ingest and place it into a separate retention tier. Anonymized aggregates and histograms are eligible for 90-day retention with automatic TTL enforcement. No user-content resides in that tier.
- Primary deletion: standard erase workflow removes data from active shards within 24–72 hours and triggers a tombstone. We can provide a signed deletion certificate once tombstone propagation completes.
- Backups/snapshots: backups are incremental and immutable for a rolling window. Our current operational practice is to keep backups for DR for up to 365 days, but we can support selective rapid-scrub processes for customer-specific erase requests. The scrub requires: (a) identifying snapshot segments that contain the tenant's data, (b) regenerating replacement snapshots for unaffected ranges, and (c) re-issuing cleaned snapshots. That work is non-trivial and we estimate an operational window of 30–90 days depending on snapshot density and retention window.

Proposed compromise language we can accept in the DPA: primary data certified deletion within 30 days; backup scrubmed and certified within 90 days after the effective deletion date, unless a legal hold is active. We will supply operational evidence (log extracts, scrub job IDs) as proof.

Irene / Naomi — flagging any regulatory objections.

—Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: erase_workflow_v2.png (diagram), scrub_job_sample.log (redacted)

--- Message 4/5 ---
From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2029 13:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions: short-lived telemetry & legal hold carveouts

Sarah —

From a compliance standpoint the technical compromise Karthik suggests is reasonable for a commercial DPA. A few clarifications we should add into the DPA and the redline:

- Definitions: explicitly define "operational telemetry" vs "customer content" and provide examples (latency histograms, anonymized error rates vs. model inputs/outputs).
- Evidence: Redwood will provide a deletion certificate for primary data and a scrub certificate for backups. Each certificate should include scrub job IDs, snapshot timestamps, and a human-readable summary of steps performed.
- Legal hold workflow: introduce a notification cadence — Redwood acknowledges receipt of preservation notice within 48 hours, provides an initial impact assessment within 5 business days, and confirms hold release and subsequent deletion schedule within 7 business days of release.
- Escrow/forensics carveout: if Acme requires forensic images for litigation hold, we need to scope that separately (operational cost + time).

If Acme signs to the primary 30 / backup 90 compromise with the above clarifications, Compliance is comfortable. We should capture the exceptions for high-sensitivity regulated data where onshore-only deletion proof is required — we can add a short appendix.

—Naomi
Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

--- Message 5/5 ---
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2029 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions: short-lived telemetry & legal hold reconciliation

Sarah — thanks for the clear asks and for moving quickly on this. Proposed consolidated language for your review (we'll drop into the shared Drive DPA redline):

1) "Operational telemetry" means non-content, aggregated operational signals (examples: latency histograms, anonymized 90th/95th percentile metrics, system error codes) and is retained up to 90 days. Operational telemetry will not contain customer-identifying inputs or outputs.

2) Primary deletion certification: Redwood certifies removal from active storage within 30 days of a deletion request and will provide a signed deletion certificate that includes the date, tombstone id(s), and a human-readable summary of actions taken.

3) Backup scrub and certification: Redwood will target backup scrub and certification within 90 days of the deletion request. Scrub scope and timing may vary with snapshot layout; Redwood will provide scrub job IDs and evidence files. If Acme requires a faster backup scrub timeline, we can discuss an SOW or higher operational tier.

4) Legal hold: Redwood will acknowledge preservation notices within 48 hours, provide an initial assessment within 5 business days, and confirm hold release and subsequent deletion schedule within 7 business days of release. Holds suspend deletion obligations until appropriate. For litigation-specific forensic imaging, scope and procurement are out-of-band.

If that aligns with Acme, I'll ask Legal to prepare a countersign-ready patch and we can route to DocuSign. I'll also attach the one-pager on deletion certification and the erase workflow diagram to the Drive link.

Action items:
- Sarah: confirm Acme accepts the 30/90 compromise or indicate required changes.
- Acme procurement/legal: if faster backup scrub SLA required, indicate willingness to include an SOW.

Thanks everyone — cc'ing Irene for contract ops.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
